body.statement:
For every realized sample, every \(a\in J\), and every measurable extended-nonnegative threshold \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), the set
\[
 \mathcal C_n(a)=\{t\in\mathbb R:Q_n(a,t)\le\widehat\kappa(a)\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
is an interval, with \(\mathbb R\) allowed when the threshold is infinite. Moreover,
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this common event, the image set in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) contains \(\tau_\zeta\), including the stated empty-set and left-endpoint conventions. Thus inversion preserves whatever probability the common LR event has; no nominal coverage probability is asserted.
body.justification: Proves convex interval structure, exact common-event equivalence, and threshold-crossing containment.
body.gap: Deterministic inversion cannot determine the common event's probability.
body.consumer: The map loses no coverage relative to a chosen threshold but makes no nominal claim.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a realized sample and a point \(a\in J\).  Put \(k=k(a)\), \(z_i=Z_{(i)}\), and define
\[
 F(v)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(z_i-v_i)^2,
 \qquad
 H_k(t)=\{v\in\mathcal C_n:v_k=t\},
 \qquad
 L_k(t)=\min_{v\in H_k(t)}F(v).
\]
For each \(t\in\mathbb R\), the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\) belongs to \(H_k(t)\), so this feasible set is nonempty.  By the definition
\[
 \mathcal C_n=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:v_1\le\cdots\le v_n\},
\]
the cone \(\mathcal C_n\) is closed and convex.  Hence \(H_k(t)\), being its intersection with the closed affine hyperplane \(\{v:v_k=t\}\), is closed and convex.  The objective \(F(v)=\lVert v-z\rVert_2^2\) is continuous and coercive on \(\mathbb R^n\).  Consequently, its minimum over the nonempty closed set \(H_k(t)\) is attained and finite.  The same argument applies to the nonempty closed cone \(\mathcal C_n\), and therefore
\[
 c_0:=\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n}F(v)=F(\widehat u)
\]
is finite and attained.  From \(H_k(t)\subseteq\mathcal C_n\) and \(\texttt{def:lr-profile}\),
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_k(t)-c_0\ge 0. \tag{1}
\]

We next show that \(t\mapsto Q_n(a,t)\) is convex.  Let \(t_1,t_2\in\mathbb R\), let \(v^{(j)}\in H_k(t_j)\) attain \(L_k(t_j)\), and fix \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).  Convexity of \(\mathcal C_n\) and linearity of the coordinate map give
\[
 \lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}
 \in H_k\bigl(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2\bigr).
\]
Since a squared Euclidean norm is convex,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 L_k\bigl(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2\bigr)
 &\le F\bigl(\lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}\bigr)\\
 &\le \lambda F(v^{(1)})+(1-\lambda)F(v^{(2)})\\
 &=\lambda L_k(t_1)+(1-\lambda)L_k(t_2).
 \end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
Subtracting the constant \(c_0\) proves the asserted convexity of \(Q_n(a,\cdot)\).

Now realize the extended-nonnegative threshold \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\).  If \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}<\infty\), then the stipulated range \(\widehat\kappa(a)\in(0,\infty)\) implies
\[
 c(a):=\widehat\kappa(a)\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\in[0,\infty).
\]
By (2), the sublevel set
\[
 \{t\in\mathbb R:Q_n(a,t)\le c(a)\}
\]
is convex and hence is an interval in \(\mathbb R\).  It is nonempty: if \(t=\widehat u_k\), then \(\widehat u\in H_k(t)\), whence
\[
 c_0\le L_k(\widehat u_k)\le F(\widehat u)=c_0,
 \qquad
 Q_n(a,\widehat u_k)=0\le c(a). \tag{3}
\]
If instead \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}=+\infty\), finiteness of \(L_k(t)\) and \(c_0\) implies \(Q_n(a,t)<\infty\) for every \(t\), so the sublevel set is all of \(\mathbb R\).  By \(\texttt{def:profile-band}\), this proves the claimed interval structure of \(\mathcal C_n(a)\), including the allowed value \(\mathbb R\).

Define the realized common profile event
\[
 E:=\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in J\}.
\]
For every \(a\in J\), positivity of \(\widehat\kappa(a)\) and \(\texttt{def:profile-band}\) give
\[
 \theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
 \le \widehat q_{n,\alpha}. \tag{4}
\]
Taking the conjunction of (4) over the nonempty interval \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\), and using the definition of a supremum together with \(\texttt{def:lr-profile}\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E
 &=\left\{\frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\text{ for every }a\in J\right\}\\
 &=\left\{\sup_{a\in J}
       \frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
       \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}\\
 &=\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}. \tag{5}
 \end{aligned}
\]
When \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}=+\infty\), both sides of (5) are the whole realized sample space, so the same equality remains valid.

Finally, on \(E\), the restriction of \(\theta\) to \(J\) selects an element of \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) at every \(a\in J\).  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\) says that \(\theta\) is nondecreasing on \([0,1]\), hence also on \(J\).  Thus \(\theta\) is one of the curves mapped in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\), and the image of this selector is
\[
 \inf\{a\in J:\theta(a)\ge\zeta\}=\tau_\zeta, \tag{6}
\]
with the same empty-set and left-endpoint conventions on both sides.  Equation (6) proves that the profile image set contains \(\tau_\zeta\) on \(E\).  The argument is deterministic conditional on the realized sample.  In particular, (5) transfers whatever probability a separately chosen threshold gives to the common event, but neither the definitions nor this proposition assign that event a nominal probability.
